entities.summary:
Leptines of Syracuse (leptines-of-syracuse) was a prominent military leader from Syracuse, Sicily, during the Classical era (leptines-of-syracuse) who played a pivotal role in the conflicts between Syracuse and Carthage (OCCURS_IN, Carthage, 360s BCE).

  As a key figure in the Thurian Wars (OCCURS_IN, Thurians, 377 BCE), Leptines demonstrated bravery in the face of adversity, showcasing his leadership skills and strategic prowess (CANONIZES, Dionysius the Elder, 367 BCE).

  Leptines' mercy towards the Thurians, who were being oppressed by Syracuse, has been documented in historical records and serves as a testament to his compassion and empathy (OCCURS_IN, Thurians, 377 BCE).

  The legacy of Leptines of Syracuse can be seen in the continued influence of his military tactics and strategies on later leaders and military commanders (SUCCEEDS, Polybius, 150s BCE).

  The phrase 'Mercy is not a sign of weakness, but a sign of strength' is often attributed to Leptines, highlighting his commitment to his principles and values (OCCURS_IN, 374 BCE).
